nations.name: Scotland
nations.summary: Every short-term let needs a council licence before taking bookings or guests. Control areas in Edinburgh and Badenoch & Strathspey. Visitor levies arriving city by city.

rules.text: All short-term lets (secondary letting, home letting, home sharing) need a licence from the local council before taking bookings or receiving guests. Operating without a licence is a criminal offence (Edinburgh notes fines up to £2,500).

Two control areas: the whole City of Edinburgh (since 5 Sep 2022) and Badenoch & Strathspey ward, Highland (since 4 Mar 2024). In these areas, using a whole dwelling that isn't your main home as a short-term let very likely needs planning permission. Licence applications there may need planning permission granted or applied for (mandatory condition 13). Proposed: Perth & Kinross agreed on 17 Jun 2026 to designate Highland Perthshire and the northern part of Eastern Perthshire. The council page (last modified 2 Jul 2026) still says it is awaiting Scottish Ministers' approval. Planning press reports that Ministers approved it on 12 Oct 2026 (UNVERIFIED: not yet on an official page we could load). Either way it is not in force until the council publishes a designation notice, at least 28 days before the start date. Argyll and Bute is consulting (21 Sep to 15 Nov 2026) on a proposed control area covering Mull and Iona; Coll and Tiree; Islay, Jura and Colonsay; and Oban, Lorn and the Inner Isles. The council extended this by two weeks after correcting figures in its consultation materials (2 Oct 2026). Not in force. Highland Council has agreed to submit further proposed control areas to Scottish Ministers (council news, Sep 2026). Reported to cover Inverness City and a wider rural area; details UNVERIFIED because the council website was offline when we checked on 22 Oct 2026. Not in force.

Edinburgh: 5% of the accommodation cost, first 5 consecutive nights, stays from 24 Jul 2026, quarterly returns via visitorlevy.scot. First returns (stays 24 Jul to 30 Sep 2026) are due 1 to 30 Oct 2026, with payment by 13 Nov 2026. Glasgow: 5% from 25 Jan 2027, whole stay, liable on bookings made from 1 Apr 2026. Highland: consultation on £5 per room per night (opened 7 Sep 2026, closes 30 Nov 2026); council decision due 10 Dec 2026, then an 18-month lead-in. Perth & Kinross: statutory consultation on a draft scheme with fixed-rate options, 19 Aug to 11 Nov 2026. No decision yet. Reported rate of £4 per room per night is UNVERIFIED (not stated on the council page). Aberdeen: 7% from 1 Apr 2027, whole stay, bookings made from 1 Oct 2026. Stirling: 3% from 14 Jun 2027, bookings made from 1 Jan 2027. West Dunbartonshire: 5% from 1 Jul 2027, bookings made from 1 Oct 2026. Dundee: consultation 31 Aug to 27 Nov 2026 on two options, £5 per room per night or 5% of the nightly room rate, both capped at 7 nights; earliest start 2028/29. Moray: consultation on whether to have a levy at all, to 31 Oct 2026 (no draft scheme yet). East Lothian: consulted on a draft 5% scheme (26 Jun to 18 Sep 2026); a council meeting on 27 Oct 2026 is asked to approve an independent review before any decision. Argyll and Bute: consultation on a flat rate per room per night closed 5 Oct 2026, no decision yet.
The UK-wide Furnished Holiday Let tax regime was abolished from April 2025. Income is now taxed as ordinary property income.

To pay non-domestic rates instead of council tax, a let must not be anyone's only or main home, must be available commercially for at least 140 nights in the financial year (1 Apr to 31 Mar), and must actually be let for at least 70 nights. Send evidence to the assessor by the later of 56 days after the year end (usually 26 May) or 56 days after their request. If you miss the deadline you pay council tax for that year. Lets to friends or family don't count. Small Business Bonus Scheme relief may apply.

nations.name: England
nations.summary: No national register yet (now expected March 2027). Use class C5 is still only a proposal. London has a 90-night cap. Business rates need 140 nights available and 70 nights let.

rules.text: A mandatory national registration scheme is coming under s.228 of the Levelling-up and Regeneration Act 2023. GOV.UK (updated 2 Oct 2026) now says it is expected to begin in March 2027. No regulations, portal or fee have been published yet.
The C5 short-term-let use class was consulted on in 2023 but is not law. Your local planning authority decides whether your letting is a material change of use. Councils can use Article 4 directions.
In Greater London, a whole home can be short-let for up to 90 nights per calendar year without planning permission. Going over that needs permission (Deregulation Act 2015, s.44).

To be rated as a business, the let must have been available for at least 140 nights and actually let for at least 70 nights in the last 12 months, and you must intend to make it available for 140 nights in the next 12. From 24 Jul 2026 there are easements for owners of 5+ lets on the same property, and for lets sharing land with another business.

On 10 Sep 2026 the government announced that mayors and Foundation Strategic Authority leaders will get the power to introduce an Overnight Visitor Levy, charged as a percentage of the accommodation cost (not a flat fee). Local leaders choose whether to use it and can offer exemptions (e.g. campsites). Accommodation providers would pay it to the authority. A bill will be introduced in due course; no levy applies yet.

The FHL regime was abolished from April 2025. From April 2027, property income (including holiday-let profits) gets its own income tax rates: 22% basic, 42% higher, 47% additional, with finance cost relief given at 22% (GOV.UK, published 26 Nov 2025).
Fire safety duties under the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005, plus gas and electrical safety, an EPC where needed, and insurance (see GOV.UK guidance).

nations.name: Wales
nations.summary: Free registration with the Welsh Revenue Authority is mandatory by 31 March 2027. Councils can start a visitor levy (£1.30 per person per night); only Cardiff has so far. Licensing is legislated for, with a default start of March 2030. Business rates need 182 days let.

rules.text: From 1 Oct 2026, anyone taking bookings of 31 nights or less must register with the Welsh Revenue Authority by 31 Mar 2027. Registration is free and applies even where no levy exists.

£1.30 per person per night (75p for hostels, dorms and tent pitches). The earliest start is 1 Apr 2027. Cardiff starts 1 Apr 2027. Councils must give 12 months' notice. Isle of Anglesey decided on 24 Sep 2026 not to introduce a levy at present, and Conwy deferred any decision the same day. Gwynedd says it has not decided yet. GOV.WALES lists Cardiff as the only council charging the levy and no councils currently consulting.
A licensing scheme for self-contained self-catering lets has Royal Assent. Its legal default commencement is March 2030, with consultation on regulations first.

To be rated as a business, a let must have been available commercially for at least 252 nights and actually let for at least 182 nights in a 12-month period, and you must intend to make it available for 252 nights in the next 12 months. Stays over 28 nights don't count towards the 182, but those nights can count towards the 252 available nights if the property could have been booked for 28 nights or less (GOV.UK guidance, corrected 9 Oct 2026). From 1 Apr 2026 (Non-Domestic Rating (Amendment of Definition of Domestic Property) (Wales) Order 2026, WSI 2026/7) you can meet the 182 nights as an average over the previous 2 or 3 years, and up to 14 nights a year donated to a registered charity count. Otherwise council tax applies, and councils can charge a second-home premium of up to 300% of the standard council tax (cap raised from 100% for 2023-24 onwards by WSI 2022/370; each council decides whether to charge one and at what level, and statutory exceptions apply).

The Welsh Government consulted (31 Jul to Fri 23 Oct 2026; now closed) on the criteria for classifying self-catering properties for local tax, including whether the 182-day letting threshold is right and 5 proposed exemptions (properties that are part of a wider business, large multi-unit properties, properties with a relevant planning restriction, properties within the curtilage of the owner's home, and properties on the owner's farm). The consultation has closed and the Welsh Government has not yet published a response or any decision, so the current rules still apply. We'll update this when the outcome is published.
Since Oct 2022 Wales has use classes C3 (main home), C5 (second home) and C6 (short-term let). Changes between them are permitted development unless an Article 4 direction applies.

nations.name: Northern Ireland
nations.summary: All tourist accommodation must hold a Tourism NI certificate. Inspections every 4 years. Fee £40 per unit (min £40, max £350).

rules.text: Under the Tourism (NI) Order 1992, all visitor accommodation needs a current Tourism NI certificate after an inspection. Certificates last 4 years. Star grading is voluntary.
Self-contained self-catering available commercially for 140 days or more a year is non-domestic (rateable).

The FHL regime was abolished UK-wide from April 2025. From April 2027, property income (including holiday-let profits) gets its own income tax rates: 22% basic, 42% higher, 47% additional, with finance cost relief given at 22% (GOV.UK, published 26 Nov 2025).

Belfast City Council is consulting (24 Aug to Mon 16 Nov 2026) on draft supplementary planning guidance for short-term lets, covering new-build and change of use of existing buildings (serviced apartments, apart-hotels, self-catering and holiday lets). The council says the draft is a material consideration in deciding planning applications. Elsewhere in NI, check with your council planning office.

councils.name: City of Edinburgh
councils.rule: Whole-city control area (planning likely needed for secondary lets). 5% visitor levy from 24 Jul 2026, capped at 5 nights. First levy returns due by 30 Oct 2026, payment by 13 Nov 2026.

councils.name: Glasgow City
councils.rule: 5% visitor levy from 25 Jan 2027 on the whole stay; applies to bookings made from 1 Apr 2026.

councils.name: Highland
councils.rule: Badenoch & Strathspey control area; council has agreed to submit further control area proposals to Ministers (details unverified). Consulting on a £5 per room per night levy until 30 Nov 2026; decision due 10 Dec 2026.

councils.name: Perth & Kinross
councils.rule: Licence fees, 3-year licence, new or renewal (Policy Statement, 10 Mar 2025). Secondary letting: £350 (1–2 guests), £530 (3–6), £900 (7–10), £1,600 (11+). Home letting/sharing: £175 / £265 / £450 / £800. Variation or transfer £75. Proposed control area (Highland Perthshire + N. Eastern Perthshire) agreed 17 Jun 2026; Ministers' approval on 12 Oct 2026 reported in planning press (UNVERIFIED); not in force until a designation notice is published. Flats already need planning permission to become a short-term let. Visitor levy: draft scheme with fixed-rate options under consultation 19 Aug to 11 Nov 2026, no decision yet (reported £4 per room per night UNVERIFIED). Public register at pkc.gov.uk/article/22511.

councils.name: Aberdeen City
councils.rule: 7% visitor levy on the whole stay from 1 Apr 2027 (bookings made from 1 Oct 2026). No control area. Licence fees from £470.40 (home sharing/letting, 1–2 guests) and £492.80 (secondary letting, 1–2 guests), effective 1 Jan 2026. No temporary licences or exemptions granted.

councils.name: Dundee City
councils.rule: No control area. Visitor levy consultation 31 Aug to 27 Nov 2026 on £5 per room per night or 5% of the room rate (both capped at 7 nights); earliest start 2028/29.

councils.name: Fife
councils.rule: No control area in force (council consulted on the principle in 2025). Visitor levy: early engagement only so far; council says the earliest a levy could start is 2028.

councils.name: Argyll and Bute
councils.rule: Consulting (21 Sep to 15 Nov 2026) on a proposed control area for Mull and Iona; Coll and Tiree; Islay, Jura and Colonsay; and Oban, Lorn and the Inner Isles. Not in force. Visitor levy consultation (flat rate per room per night proposed) closed 5 Oct 2026; no decision yet. 3-year licence from £285.30 (home sharing/letting, up to 4 guests) or £398.95 (secondary letting, up to 4 guests).

councils.name: Stirling
councils.rule: 3% visitor levy from 14 Jun 2027 (bookings made from 1 Jan 2027); Stirling residents and nights beyond 7 refunded. No control area. Licence fees from £113 (home letting/sharing, up to 4) and £283 (secondary letting, up to 4), as published for 2025-26.

councils.name: West Dunbartonshire
councils.rule: 5% visitor levy on the whole stay from 1 Jul 2027 (bookings made and paid for from 1 Oct 2026). No control area. Licence grant or renewal £929.

councils.name: Greater London (all boroughs)
councils.rule: 90 nights per calendar year whole-home cap without planning permission.

councils.name: Cornwall
councils.rule: 100% council tax second-home premium from 1 Apr 2025, with exceptions (e.g. holiday-only planning conditions).

councils.name: Gwynedd
councils.rule: Article 4 direction (C3 to C5/C6) quashed. Not in force since the Court of Appeal refused appeal on 6 Feb 2026. Visitor levy: consulted May to Jul 2026; council says no decision yet.

councils.name: Cardiff
councils.rule: Visitor levy from 1 Apr 2027 (£1.30 per person per night).

councils.name: Pembrokeshire
councils.rule: Council tax second-home premium of 125% from 1 Apr 2026 (on top of the standard charge), down from 150% in 2025-26. Premium for 2027-28 was due to be set by full Council on 15 Oct 2026; local press reports 125% was kept (UNVERIFIED).

councils.name: Isle of Anglesey
councils.rule: No visitor levy: Full Council decided on 24 Sep 2026 not to introduce one at present. Council tax second-home premium kept at 100% for 2026-27 (so a second home pays double).

councils.name: Conwy
councils.rule: Visitor levy decision deferred by Full Council on 24 Sep 2026. Council tax second-home premium of 150% (250% of the standard bill) kept for 2026-27 and 2027-28.

councils.name: Ceredigion
councils.rule: Council tax second-home premium of 150% (250% of the standard bill) since 1 Apr 2025, covering second homes and self-catering units not in business rates. No visitor levy decision found.

councils.name: Powys
councils.rule: Council tax second-home premium of 75% (175% of the standard bill), in place since 1 Apr 2023 and unchanged for 2026-27. No visitor levy at this stage; any levy left to the council elected in May 2027, earliest start 2028.

councils.name: East Lothian
councils.rule: Licence needed. No control area, but check planning before applying. Draft 5% visitor levy consulted on (26 Jun to 18 Sep 2026); a 27 Oct 2026 council meeting is asked to approve an independent review before any decision.

councils.name: Moray
councils.rule: Licence needed (£540 new or renewal from 1 Apr 2026). No control area. Consultation on whether to have a visitor levy at all runs to 31 Oct 2026; no decision made.

councils.name: Scottish Borders
councils.rule: Licence needed (3-year licence, £417 to £537 by guest numbers). No control area. No visitor levy proposed.

councils.name: Aberdeenshire
councils.rule: Licence needed (3-year licence, £364 to £1,006 by guest numbers and licence type). No control area. No visitor levy scheme proposed yet.

councils.name: Dumfries and Galloway
councils.rule: Licence needed (3-year licence, £324 to £454 by guest numbers and licence type). No control area. Visitor levy plans dropped in June 2026.

councils.name: North Yorkshire
councils.rule: 100% council tax premium on second homes (200% bill) since 1 Apr 2025, kept unchanged for 2026-27. Holiday lets that qualify for business rates (140 nights available, 70 let) pay business rates instead. No licensing or local registration scheme.

councils.name: Northumberland
councils.rule: 100% council tax premium on second homes (200% bill) since 1 Apr 2025. Holiday lets that qualify for business rates (140 nights available, 70 let) pay business rates instead. No licensing or local registration scheme.

councils.name: Westmorland and Furness
councils.rule: 100% council tax premium on second homes (200% bill) since 1 Apr 2025, with national and local discretionary exceptions. Holiday lets that qualify for business rates (140 nights available, 70 let) pay business rates instead. No licensing or local registration scheme.

councils.name: Cumberland
councils.rule: 100% council tax premium on second homes (200% bill) since 1 Apr 2025. Holiday lets that qualify for business rates (140 nights available, 70 let) pay business rates instead. No licensing or local registration scheme.

councils.name: North Norfolk
councils.rule: 100% council tax premium on second homes (200% bill) since 1 Apr 2025. Holiday lets that qualify for business rates (140 nights available, 70 let) pay business rates instead. No licensing or local registration scheme.

councils.name: Dorset
councils.rule: 100% council tax premium on second homes (200% bill) since 1 Apr 2025. Holiday lets that qualify for business rates (140 nights available, 70 let) pay business rates instead. No licensing or local registration scheme.

councils.name: South Hams
councils.rule: 100% council tax premium on second homes (200% bill) since 1 Apr 2025, plus local discretionary exceptions. Holiday lets that qualify for business rates (140 nights available, 70 let) pay business rates instead. No licensing or local registration scheme.

councils.name: North Devon
councils.rule: 100% council tax premium on second homes (200% bill) since 1 Apr 2025. Holiday lets that qualify for business rates (140 nights available, 70 let) pay business rates instead. No licensing or local registration scheme.

councils.name: Isle of Wight
councils.rule: 100% council tax premium on second homes (200% bill) since 1 Apr 2025. Holiday lets that qualify for business rates (140 nights available, 70 let) pay business rates instead. No licensing or local registration scheme.

councils.name: Denbighshire
councils.rule: 150% council tax premium on second homes (250% bill), kept from 1 Apr 2026. Holiday lets need free WRA registration by 31 Mar 2027. No visitor levy.

councils.name: Carmarthenshire
councils.rule: 100% council tax premium on second homes (200% bill) since 1 Apr 2025. Holiday lets need free WRA registration by 31 Mar 2027. No visitor levy.

councils.name: Swansea
councils.rule: 100% council tax premium on second homes (200% bill) since 1 Apr 2021. Holiday lets need free WRA registration by 31 Mar 2027. No visitor levy.

councils.name: Falkirk
councils.rule: Licence needed (£157.50 to £504 on the 2025/26 table). No control area. Consultation on a 5% visitor levy runs to 25 Nov 2026; full Council expected to decide in January 2027.

councils.name: Orkney Islands
councils.rule: Licence needed (£275 to £583 for 3 years, 25% off on non-linked isles). No control area. Council decided against an overnight visitor levy on 23 Sep 2025.

councils.name: Shetland Islands
councils.rule: Licence needed (£210 to £530 by guest numbers, 2026/27). No control area. Council decided against an overnight visitor levy in Sep 2025.

councils.name: Na h-Eileanan Siar (Western Isles)
councils.rule: Licence needed (base fee £189 or £294 plus £21 per guest, 2026/27). No control area. Accommodation-based visitor levy paused.

councils.name: South Ayrshire
councils.rule: Licence needed (£300 or £480 for a new secondary let, by guest numbers). No control area, but every application includes a planning operational statement. Visitor levy work paused until August 2027 at the earliest.

councils.name: Angus
councils.rule: Licence needed (£349 to £588 by guest numbers; 3-year grant, renewals up to 6 years). No control area. No visitor levy: the council is still at early engagement.

councils.name: North Ayrshire
councils.rule: Licence needed (£300 or £480 for a new secondary let, by guest numbers; covers Arran and Cumbrae). No control area. No visitor levy decided yet. Second homes pay double council tax since April 2025.

changes.text: Added a council page for North Ayrshire, including Arran and Cumbrae (licence £300 or £480 for a new secondary let from 1 April 2026; no control area; visitor levy not yet decided).

Added a free "Is your licence renewal due?" checker for Scottish short-term let licences: estimates your expiry date and when to start your renewal, with renewal rules from the 1982 Act, Scottish Government guidance and council pages (Highland, Edinburgh, Argyll and Bute, Na h-Eileanan Siar, Angus).

Added council pages for South Ayrshire (visitor levy paused until August 2027 at the earliest; licensing policy and fees under review) and Angus (licence £349 to £588, renewals now up to 6 years; no control area), with licence fees and levy status.

Added 4 Scottish council pages: Falkirk (5% visitor levy consultation open to 25 Nov 2026), Orkney Islands, Shetland Islands and Na h-Eileanan Siar (Western Isles), with 2026/27 licence fees and levy status. The three island councils are not pursuing an overnight levy.

Added 8 council pages for holiday-let hotspots: North Norfolk, Dorset, South Hams, North Devon, Isle of Wight (100% second homes premium from 1 Apr 2025), Denbighshire (150%), Carmarthenshire (100%) and Swansea (100%), plus a free licence and registration checker.

Welsh Government consultation on how self-catering properties are classified for local tax (including the 182-day letting threshold and 5 proposed exemptions) closed. No response or decision published yet; current rules still apply.

GOV.UK Wales business rates guidance corrected: nights in stays over 28 nights don't count towards the 182 let nights, but can count towards the 252 available nights if the property could have been booked for 28 nights or less.
WRA registration guidance updated: register by 31 Mar 2027.
National STL register start pushed to 'expected March 2027'.
Argyll and Bute corrects figures in its control area consultation and extends it by two weeks, to 15 Nov 2026.
Duty to register visitor accommodation with the WRA starts.
Aberdeen (7%) and West Dunbartonshire (5%) visitor levies: bookings made from today are liable for stays from 1 Apr 2027 and 1 Jul 2027.
Business rates guidance adds rules for owners of 5+ lets and for mixed-use sites (effective 24 Jul 2026).
Isle of Anglesey decides not to introduce a visitor levy at present; Conwy defers any decision. Cardiff remains the only Welsh council charging the levy.
Argyll and Bute opens consultation (to 15 Nov 2026) on a proposed short-term let control area covering Mull and Iona; Coll and Tiree; Islay, Jura and Colonsay; and Oban, Lorn and the Inner Isles.
Government announces an Overnight Visitor Levy power for mayors and Foundation Strategic Authorities (percentage of room cost; needs legislation).
Highland opens 12-week visitor levy consultation (£5 per room per night proposed).
Moray opens a consultation on whether to introduce a visitor levy (to 31 Oct 2026).
Dundee opens a 12-week visitor levy consultation on two options: £5 per room per night or 5% of the room rate, both capped at 7 nights (to 27 Nov 2026).
Belfast City Council consults on draft planning guidance for short-term lets (to 16 Nov 2026).
Perth & Kinross opens 12-week consultation on a draft visitor levy.
Welsh Government opens consultation on the 182-day self-catering rates rule and 5 proposed exemptions (closes Fri 23 Oct 2026).
Edinburgh 5% visitor levy goes live.
Perth & Kinross agrees STL control area for Highland Perthshire and N. Eastern Perthshire (awaiting Ministers).
Gwynedd Article 4 direction ends after appeal refused.
